content.rationale: The undo verb: a leading --help answers with the verb's own text (xlvoxmyl/rwlywqrk, per oqnsuzqu) and any other argument refuses, named (U1, puuvpqzl); otherwise it loads the marker state (M-markers-persist, wzyorrny), answers with the state undo leaves — the undone count one further back and the position at the pre-boundary of the operation it undoes (S5-undo-effect, zuqzrlrx) — restores that position through the restore module (znmsuqlm, S3-restore kttmwrsv's mechanism), a crossing that cannot spawn or fails refusing with its reason and naming the boundary, and then writes the state it leaves (S5-save-after-restore, kqqysmxn), so the restore cannot take the record of the operation with it. Most-recent-not-already-undone scope, no-selector and the restore-boundary existence are D15's (lummwqtx, yrnkmrqx, utplmmvz), whole-operation scope D8a's (prsoxsuo) over D8b's boundary pairs (txqmnvup), and never a partial restore is qmynqmwy's. A marker file that cannot be read refuses, naming the corruption (S5-refusal-site, tkqvkzsy), and a marker file that cannot be read or written refuses through the invocation that touched it (S2-markers-refusal-site, sprvousp); nothing left to undo and a count or bound past the pairs refuse inside M-markers-guards (lqtqzznn). The invocation never brackets (S5-lifecycle, vwlrqoxk) and writes nothing on success (O7-undo, tmxutlwm). It takes the injected context (M-context zttrwlts, M-context-injection ryuswoxz) and returns its lines — none on success — for the envelope to write (M-output-return, utrzvyyt) under M-route's handler shape (ynvwvzrm). I1-serde (orrvsxqq) fixes the JSON layer the module is written against — serde and serde_json, the crate's own `Value` and the derive. It takes the store through the context's fallible accessor (S3-root-required).
